meta.title: Forge — How idempotency keys ended duplicate jobs
meta.description: Engineering talk from the Forge jobs API team: why client retries ran jobs twice, how server-side idempotency keys work, what they cost in latency and storage, and what we would change.

slides.heading: Idempotency keys cut our duplicate jobs from 2.1% to 0.003%.
slides.lead: What broke, what we built, and what it cost.
slides.notes: Thesis first. Every slide after this is evidence for that one number.

slides.heading: A timeout plus a retry ran each job twice
slides.lead: The gateway gave up at 30 s. The worker did not.

steps.body: Did the fix cost us latency?

slides.heading: 84% of duplicate jobs came from SDK retries after a timeout
slides.lead: Source: 6,140 duplicate jobs traced in job logs, March–May 2026.

slides.heading: The server stores the first response under the key for 24 hours
slides.image: data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 450 750'><rect width='450' height='750' fill='%23161b22'/><g font-family='JetBrains Mono,Menlo,monospace' font-size='20'><rect x='45' y='90' width='360' height='80' rx='10' fill='%230d1117' stroke='%2358a6ff' stroke-width='3'/><text x='70' y='138' fill='%23e6edf3'>POST + key run_0730</text><path d='M225 170 V230' stroke='%238b949e' stroke-width='3'/><rect x='45' y='230' width='360' height='80' rx='10' fill='%230d1117' stroke='%2358a6ff' stroke-width='3'/><text x='70' y='278' fill='%23e6edf3'>key seen before?</text><path d='M140 310 V380 M310 310 V380' stroke='%238b949e' stroke-width='3'/><text x='70' y='360' fill='%233fb950'>no</text><text x='325' y='360' fill='%23d29922'>yes</text><rect x='30' y='380' width='190' height='120' rx='10' fill='%230d1117' stroke='%233fb950' stroke-width='3'/><text x='50' y='428' fill='%233fb950'>run job,</text><text x='50' y='460' fill='%233fb950'>save reply</text><rect x='235' y='380' width='190' height='120' rx='10' fill='%230d1117' stroke='%23d29922' stroke-width='3'/><text x='255' y='428' fill='%23d29922'>return</text><text x='255' y='460' fill='%23d29922'>saved reply</text><text x='45' y='590' fill='%238b949e'>TTL 24 h · Redis</text><text x='45' y='625' fill='%238b949e'>1 row per key</text></g></svg>
slides.imageAlt: Flow: a POST with an idempotency key is checked. A new key runs the job and saves the reply; a seen key returns the saved reply.
slides.body: First request with a key runs the job and saves the reply. Any retry with the same key gets that saved reply, not a new job.

slides.heading: Did the fix cost us latency?
Duplicates fell 700× while p99 latency rose only 4 ms
slides.left:
Duplicate rate: 2.1%
p99 create latency: 182 ms
Incidents: 9
slides.right:
Duplicate rate: 0.003%
p99 create latency: 186 ms
Incidents: 0
slides.notes: Let the room do the maths on 2.1 over 0.003. Then point at the 4 ms: that is the whole cost.

slides.heading: One field on create makes every retry safe
slides.notes: Point at the key. It comes from the batch, not from a random UUID; a random key per retry defeats the whole design.

slides.heading: Keys cost 38 GB of Redis and do not cover long jobs
We would ship keys in the SDK on day one, not in year two
slides.body: Two years of retries ran without keys. 9 incidents and 6,140 duplicate jobs came from that gap.
slides.aside: Rule now: every write endpoint ships with an idempotency key.

slides.heading: Make every write safe to retry, and duplicates disappear.
slides.lead: Slides, code and the incident write-up are on the Forge engineering blog.
